newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Coca-Cola plans Zimbabwe expansion - sources.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola plans Zimbabwe expansion - sources.

text.p: U.S. soft drinks giant Coca-Cola is to invest $60 million in the next three years in Zimbabwe as part of plans to expand its business throughout Africa, industry sources said on Monday.

Coca-Cola Co president and chief operating officer Doug Ivester, who earlier announced the company and its seven South African bottlers would invest 1.25 billion rand in South Africa over the next five years, declined to detail investment plans for other African countries, including Zimbabwe.
He said announcements would be made in the appropriate countries.
Ivester flies to Zimbabwe on Tuesday and he is expected to announce details of expansion plans there.

"You're looking at a substantial investment in Zimbabwe, about $60 million," one of source said, adding this was targeted at one of its bottlers which had been strapped for fresh resources "for some time".
Ivester is also scheduled to visit Kenya and Tanzania.
